test_title: PYST 38 - SSC CHSL 2025 - General Awareness (Held On: 26 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To respect one's parents and teachers
To take part in village panchayat

solution:
The correct answer is __**To safeguard public property**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Fundamental Duties** are enshrined in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution, added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**. These duties are meant to promote a sense of responsibility and discipline among citizens. 
• The duty **“To safeguard public property”** is explicitly mentioned under the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution. It emphasizes citizens' role in protecting and conserving public infrastructure and national assets. 
• The Fundamental Duties were inspired by the **Soviet Constitution** and aim to inculcate civic and moral values in Indian citizens. 
• Examples of safeguarding public property include protecting historical monuments, public transportation, government buildings, and preventing vandalism or misuse. 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-enforceable by law but are crucial for the nation's collective welfare and ethical governance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Article 51A and Fundamental Duties:** 
• **Article 51A** lists **11 Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens. These were introduced through the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1976**. 
• Some of the Fundamental Duties include **respecting the Constitution**, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and safeguarding public property. 
• The **86th Amendment Act, 2002** added the duty for parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to children aged **6-14 years**. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the **USSR (Soviet Union)** and other socialist countries. 
• They were introduced during the tenure of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi** to counteract the growing indiscipline and foster a sense of responsibility among citizens. 
• **Legal Framework:** 
• Though Fundamental Duties are **non-justiciable**, laws can be enacted to enforce them indirectly. For instance, laws against vandalism protect public property. 
• Some Fundamental Duties have been linked to legal provisions such as the **Environmental Protection Act, 1986**, which aligns with the duty to protect the natural environment. 
• **Comparison with Fundamental Rights:** 
• While Fundamental Rights grant privileges and freedoms to citizens, Fundamental Duties emphasize moral obligations. 
• Rights and Duties are interconnected, as enjoying rights comes with the responsibility to perform duties for the welfare of society. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Fundamental Duties in Detail:** 
• There are a total of **11 Fundamental Duties**, which include respecting national symbols, promoting harmony, and protecting the environment. 
• The duty to safeguard public property ensures the integrity and functionality of assets vital to public welfare. 
• **Examples of Safeguarding Public Property:** 
• Participating in campaigns against vandalism. 
• Ensuring responsible use of public transport and facilities. 
• Encouraging awareness about the importance of conserving national heritage sites. 
• **Significance of Fundamental Duties:** 
• They act as a **moral compass** for citizens, promoting national unity and responsibility. 
• They complement Fundamental Rights by instilling a sense of accountability towards the nation. 
3d
